findings.doc_quote: ChangeType is a union of literal value, C.* condition instance, glob string, or callable (value) -> bool .
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/types/types.py:330 — "FalseySentinel | V | Condition[V | FalseySentinel] | ComparisonCondition[V | FalseySentinel] | None"
findings.explanation: The alias has no glob-string member, and a string in this position gets no glob handling in general. Only P.ServiceDataWhere (auto_glob) wraps glob strings. The alias also includes sentinels, None, and two-argument comparison conditions, which the sentence omits.
findings.suggested_fix: ChangeType is a union of literal value, C.* condition instance, or callable (value) -> bool. A string is matched literally unless wrapped in C.Glob; only P.ServiceDataWhere auto-detects globs.

findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/event_handling/predicates.py:157 — `fn: "Predicate[EventT]"`. Runtime: P.Guard(predicate=...) raises TypeError: Guard.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'predicate'
findings.explanation: The dataclass field is named `fn`, not `predicate`. Passing the documented keyword raises TypeError. Positional use works.

findings.doc_quote: condition accepts a literal value, a C.* condition instance, a glob string, or any callable (value) -> bool .
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/event_handling/predicates.py:763-765 — `if not callable(condition): ... return coerce_to_literal_type(actual, condition) == condition`. Runtime: compare_value("light.kitchen", "light.*") returns False
findings.explanation: P.ValueIs does not auto-detect globs. A bare glob string is compared by plain equality, so P.ValueIs(source=A.get_entity_id, condition="light.*") never matches a real entity. The same applies to P.StateFrom, P.StateTo, P.AttrFrom, P.AttrTo and changed_to=/changed_from= (src/hassette/bus/bus.py:1758-1764 passes the value through unwrapped). Glob detection exists only in DomainMatches, EntityMatches and ServiceMatches (predicates.py:227-229) and in ServiceDataWhere (predicates.py:700).
findings.suggested_fix: condition accepts a literal value, a C.* condition instance, or any callable (value) -> bool. A glob string is compared literally here; wrap it in C.Glob to match as a pattern.

findings.doc_quote: When old_state is None , returns False even if the attribute is present on the new state.
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/event_handling/predicates.py:530-531 — `if value.payload.data.old_state is None: return get_attr_new(self.attr_name)(value) is not MISSING_VALUE`. Runtime: returns True when the attribute is present, False when absent
findings.explanation: The behavior is the opposite of the claim. With no old state, the predicate returns True when the attribute exists on new_state, and False only when it is absent.
findings.suggested_fix: When old_state is None, returns True if the attribute is present on the new state, and False if it is absent.

findings.doc_quote: Returns True when the string value contains substring , ignoring case.
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/event_handling/conditions.py:227 — `return isinstance(value, str) and self.substring in value`. Runtime: C.Contains("KIT")("kitchen") returns False
findings.explanation: The match is case-sensitive. No case folding happens anywhere in the class.
findings.suggested_fix: Returns True when the string value contains substring (case-sensitive).

findings.doc_quote: collection must be a sequence, not a string. Passing a string raises TypeError .
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/event_handling/conditions.py:120-122 — `if isinstance(collection, str): raise ValueError("collection must be a sequence of values, not a string")`. Runtime: C.IsIn, C.NotIn, C.Intersects and C.NotIntersects all raise ValueError when given "abc"
findings.explanation: All four collection conditions raise ValueError, so code catching TypeError would not catch it.
findings.suggested_fix: collection must be a sequence, not a string. Passing a string raises ValueError.

findings.doc_quote: Returns True when float(old) < threshold <= float(new) .
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/event_handling/conditions.py:611 — `return float(old_value) <= self.threshold < float(new_value)`. Runtime: CrossedAbove(25)("25","26") returns True; CrossedAbove(25)("24","25") returns False
findings.explanation: The boundaries are reversed. An old value equal to the threshold counts as below it, and a new value equal to the threshold does not count as crossed. A reading landing exactly on the threshold does not fire, contrary to the page.
findings.suggested_fix: Returns True when float(old) <= threshold < float(new).

findings.doc_quote: The context dict from the event payload.
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/events/base.py:31-37 — `@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True) class HassContext: id: str; parent_id: str | None; user_id: str | None`
findings.explanation: The accessor returns a frozen HassContext dataclass, not a dict. Fields are read as attributes, so subscript access such as ctx["id"] fails. The Returns column on the same row correctly says HassContext.
findings.suggested_fix: The HassContext object from the event payload.

findings.doc_quote: Excludes last_reported , last_updated , and last_changed by default.
findings.explanation: The default exclusion list also contains context, which the page omits. A context-only difference does not appear in the diff.
findings.suggested_fix: Excludes last_reported, last_updated, last_changed, and context by default.

summary: The page is mostly accurate: accessor tables, literal coercion, operator composition, sentinels, and most signatures all match the code. Nine claims fail, and the errors cluster in predicate and condition descriptions: the Guard parameter name, AttrDidChange with no old state, C.Contains case sensitivity, the C.CrossedAbove boundaries, and the exception for string collections. The most misleading is the implied glob-string support on P.ValueIs and everything built on it, because a bare glob there is compared literally and silently never matches.
